title: Correct energy value
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (1) must be 3.24 J (or equivalent).

title: Correct flux expression
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (2) must be \(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{5000\pi} \mathrm{Wb}\) (or an equivalent symbolic/numeric form).

title: Uses effective EMF
description: Important: The solution must correctly convert the peak EMF from the graph to an RMS/effective value using \(E = E_m / \sqrt{2}\).

title: Applies circuit power law
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply power/energy formulas for the circuit, such as \(P = U^2/R\) or \(Q = (U^2/R)t\), where \(U\) is the terminal voltage across the bulb.

title: Relates EMF to flux
description: Important: For part (2), the solution must connect the peak EMF to magnetic flux via \(E_m = nBS\omega = n\Phi_m \omega\), and determine \(\omega\) from the period.

title: Determines period
description: Optional: The solution may explicitly read the period (T = 0.02 s) from the provided graph to find the angular frequency.

title: Consistent unit handling
description: Optional: The solution demonstrates consistent use and conversion of units (e.g., seconds, webers, joules).

title: Misinterprets peak EMF
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses the peak EMF (6√2 V) directly in power calculations without converting to an effective value.

title: Confuses terminal and EMF
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly uses the source EMF (E) instead of the terminal voltage across the bulb (U) in the power formula.

title: Sign or phase error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly handles the sinusoidal phase or sign when calculating the magnetic flux at the specified instant.
